title: Distributed Tracing Explained: OpenTelemetry + Jaeger in 60 Seconds 🔍 #shorts
description:
Your checkout takes 2 seconds, but it touches 5 services. Which one is slow? Metrics tell you something is wrong; distributed tracing tells you where. OpenTelemetry gives every request a trace ID that's passed along in headers to every service it touches. Each service records a span with its start time and duration, the spans are sent to Jaeger, and Jaeger draws them as a waterfall timeline, so the slow step stands out instantly.

lines: Your checkout takes two seconds. But one click touches five different services.
Metrics tell you something is wrong. Distributed tracing tells you exactly where.
With OpenTelemetry, every request gets a unique trace ID, and it's passed along in the headers to every service the request touches.
Each service records a span: what it did, when it started, and how long it took. Spans can have child spans, like a database query inside a service.
All the spans are sent to Jaeger, which lines them up into a waterfall. And there it is: the payment service spent 1.6 seconds waiting on the bank.
One trace ID. Many spans. Find the slow part in seconds.
